# V1 Mission — iteration log (append-only)

One entry per mission-control iteration, newest LAST (append). Fixed template — keep every
section, write "none" rather than omitting:

```markdown
## N — YYYY-MM-DD — <headline>
**Picked**: <backlog item + why it was top>
**Reality check**: <what git/code verification of the doc's status found>
**Shipped**: <commits/branches/PRs, evaluator result + score, or "parked: reason">
**Routing evidence**: model=<m> task-class=<design|plan|execute|evaluate|mechanical>
  round1-score=<n> rounds=<n> corrections=<n>
  provider=<p> agent=<a> cost=<$<n>|quota-bucket:weekly-fable|quota-bucket:weekly-opus|unknown>
  <!-- provider/agent/cost appended 2026-07-16 (M2). Leading columns unchanged so historical rows
       still parse. provider = anthropic|codex|gemini|motoko|... ; agent = claude-code|codex|... ;
       cost = $ for metered providers (executResult.CostUSD), quota-bucket:<weekly-*> for Anthropic
       subscription calls, explicit "unknown" otherwise — NEVER silent 0 (Critical Principle 2). -->
**Ruled out**: <hypotheses/approaches refuted this iteration — the anti-re-chase ledger>
**Retro lane**: <skill-fix: file+change | process-fix: change | backlog: new doc | none>
**Next**: <what iteration N+1 should pick up>
```

**Diagnosis (data before conclusions, Standing rule 5)**: (1) parser + `internal/parser/testdata` + fuzz
test UNCHANGED for 7 days; (2) the previous **11** dev CI runs were green on the same parser code (incl.
the identical-class `3b77bc036` data commit); (3) local repro `go test -fuzz=FuzzParseExpr -fuzztime=2s`
**PASS 3/3** (~3.2–3.4s wall); (4) **no crasher persisted** (a timeout is not a panic — Go doesn't write
a `testdata/fuzz` seed for it); (5) the CI log shows **4 workers** vs 16 locally. Root cause: when
`-fuzztime=2s` expires while a slow, deeply-nested input (DELIM_STACK depth 9 in the log) is mid-execution
on a loaded 4-worker runner, Go's fuzzing coordinator cancels the worker context and reports the
cancellation as a test **FAIL** — a known fuzztime-boundary artifact, not a parser bug.

**Fix (fix-forward, small — Gate 1)**: `make fuzz-parser` now discriminates a **real crasher**
(`Failing input written to testdata/fuzz/…` → fail immediately, `exit $$rc`) from the **transient boundary
timeout** (`context deadline exceeded` with no crasher → retry once); a genuine slow-parse regression that
*always* times out still fails on the second attempt (`exit 1`). Crash-detection AND perf-regression
coverage preserved; only the single-boundary flake is masked. `make fuzz-parser` PASS locally post-patch.
Commit `c8f61e212` (`make/test.mk` + CHANGELOG), pushed direct-to-dev (clean tree, no `MERGE_HEAD`).

**Gate-3b (bounded, 30-min cap)**: CI run `29632296716` on `c8f61e212` → **completed success** @ 07:38

**Reality check + method**: the question is answerable ENTIRELY from banked code + the reuse benchmark already run in `27cead433` (2026-07-18). **Deliberately did NOT re-run the live test** — a fresh `TestLiveEnvironmentReuseEconomics`/E2E is ~$0.11–0.87 metered, i.e. the exact "cost going crazy" Mark is worried about; the banked data answers all three sub-questions. **Iteration metered spend: $0.00** (all local code reads + git + gh). Verified the cost path by reading source, not by spending.

**Answer delivered (code-grounded):**
- **(1) Verified per-call?** The TOKEN COUNTS are real per-call telemetry — the Managed Agents API returns cumulative usage in the terminal `interaction.completed` SSE event (`state.Usage.Total{Input,Output,Thought}Tokens`, `internal/executor/managed_agents/managed_agents.go:264-265`). The DOLLAR figure is **NOT a Google invoice** — it's computed **client-side**: `CostModel()` (`:97-103`, hardcoded gemini-3-5-flash Vertex list rates) × `CalculateCost` (`internal/executor/executor.go:319-329`, `tokens/1000 × per-1K-rate`). So: real per-call usage × fixed list price.
- **(2) Costing basis:** `InputTokens × $1.50/1M + (Output+Thought)Tokens × $9.00/1M` (thought/reasoning tokens billed at output rate). For the $0.865 run: `527221 in ×$1.50/1M = $0.791 (91%) + 8201 out ×$9.00/1M = $0.074 (9%)` = $0.865 ✓ (matches the reported $0.864641).
- **(3) Boot cost — Mark's intuition is directionally right:** 91% of the cost is INPUT tokens = the agentic context accumulated across turns (system prompt + tool defs + repeated tool-result replay), NOT reasoning output. BUT the $0.87 was **not a floor** — it was a *loose-directive* one-off E2E. The reuse benchmark measured the two levers: **tight directive** ("run exactly these, don't explore") collapses cost **~12×** ($0.87→$0.07 — the 527K was agent wandering); **environment reuse** (persist the sandbox FS, skip the clone/boot) saves a further **42.4%** ($0.068→$0.039, FS persistence SHA-verified). Operational escalation cost **$0.04–0.15**, both levers now MANDATORY for gemini runs (per `27cead433`).
- **Honesty caveat flagged:** the client-side figure bills every input token at full **non-cached** list price — the API doesn't report cache reads (`CacheReadInputTokens: 0 // Not reported by Managed Agents API`, `:266`), so if Vertex applies server-side context caching the real Google invoice is **lower**; our $0.86 is a conservative UPPER bound.
- **Record corrected:** iter-53's fleet-role report quoted "~$0.86/run" as the gemini *evaluator* cost — that **overstates the operational cost ~6–12×** (real evaluator run with the mandatory tight-directive + env-reuse levers ≈ $0.07–0.15). This de-risks the still-parked gemini fleet-role decision.
- **Guardrails already in place** (Mark's "make sure costs don't go crazy", landed `27cead433`): `MISSION_METERED_BUDGET_USD=$5` per-iteration ceiling + per-call caps (quorum $0.10/reviewer; codex mid-stream CostBudget kill; managed_agents post-hoc over-budget flag) + the two mandatory cost levers. Cost gate for managed_agents is **post-hoc only** (no step-level token counts → no mid-stream kill-on-cost — API limitation, `:294-322`).

Can we conceivably run it every turn after .ail files are written by say Motoko or on a hook in other coding harnesses?"* — a follow-up to iter-56's landed `m-ailang-fmt` (Phase 1). This is a QUESTION answerable from banked code + a cheap live reproduction, so the deliverable is **answer + decomposition + record** (the iter-53/55/60 pattern), NOT a sprint. **Gate-0/1**: killswitch armed; billing **CLEAN** (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`/`AUTH_TOKEN` both empty); gh `sunholo-voight-kampff`; tree clean on dev, no `MERGE_HEAD`; bookkeeping issue **#399**. No weekly rotation (#399 created 2026-07-16, after the most-recent Monday 07-13 boundary; 31 comments < 80). Inbox: 1 informational `eval-suite` "started" notice, ack'd (not a regression/directive).

**Findings (all reproduced at HEAD, `ailang v0.29.2-421-g81a45f2d8`, rebuilt via `make quick-install`)**:
1. **Discoverability = NO.** `ailang prompt --source=embedded` (v0.16.2) teaches `ailang check` / `ailang run` (×22) / `ailang test` but has **zero** mention of the `ailang fmt` command — every "fmt"/"format" grep hit is a string-formatting *function* (`formatRFC3339`, etc.), not the CLI. An agent reading the teaching prompt would not know `ailang fmt` exists. (`ailang fmt --help` itself is complete — the gap is the teaching prompt, not the CLI help.)
2. **Auto-run-every-turn = near-useless PRE-Phase-2.** Phase-1 fmt **fails-closed on any comment-bearing file** (exit 2, byte-identical — reproduced: a 3-line file with one `--` comment → `Error: comments are not yet supported by ailang fmt`; a comment-free file formats cleanly). Corpus impact: **344/393 (87.5%) of `examples/*.ail` contain comments → un-formattable today**; only 49 (12.5%) are comment-free. Neither `--write` (rewrite) nor `--check` (CI drift) is usable on real agent-written code — a per-turn PostToolUse/Motoko hook would exit-2/no-op on ~7 of every 8 files, giving false confidence.
3. **Both threads converge on the same unlock:** Phase-2 lossless comment preservation, **already fully designed** in the shipped doc (`implemented/v0_30_0/m-ailang-fmt.md` §168-332 "Lossless Attachment", est. 2–3d, quorum-reviewed as part of the parent). Until it lands, teaching agents to run fmt would frustrate them (refusal on their own commented code) and an auto-hook is a no-op — so the disciplined sequencing is **Phase-2 first, then adoption** (no premature adoption).

**Deliverable (doc-only, no code)**: (a) answered Mark on #399 with the above; (b) queued two DX sub-items under the fmt cluster — **m-ailang-fmt-phase2** (NEW-DOC candidate, the unblock; design pre-exists → refine-into-planned, not a fresh designer run) and **m-ailang-fmt-adoption** (NEW-DOC candidate, GATED behind phase2: prompt line + CLI discoverability + opt-in harness hooks) — both awaiting Mark's greenlight on priority; (c) STATUS stamp (iter-58 added, iter-55 aged out per newest-3 rule); (d) this log entry.

Both reviewers raised CORRECT soundness defects my controller PASS under-weighted: (gemini) §3 default plan is UNSOUND — masking the *state* to 63 bits does NOT prevent sign corruption because intermediate multiplies (`z * 0xBF58…`) overflow into the sign bit BEFORE the shift, so `z >> 27` still sign-extends; the `lsr` helper is off-by-one (`63-k` should be `64-k`); 63-bit masking breaks standard-SplitMix64 interop → defeats the doc's headline benchmark payoff. (gpt5-6-sol) the SplitMix64 constants exceed signed-63-bit positive range and are unverified to parse; `int_range` rejection is unbounded + `hi-lo+1` overflow + `lo>hi` undefined. **Controller live-confirmed the parse failure**: `0x9E3779B97F4A7C15` → "could not parse as integer" at HEAD (lexer uses signed ParseInt).

Rather than inherit the queue row's claim, the controller rebuilt both binaries and ran a 9-fixture matrix at HEAD, finding **three coupled defects, not one**: (1) the known blocker (`!{Rand[mode=seeded|crypto]}` cannot call the bare `std/rand` wrappers; explicit `mode=os` control passes); (2) the rejection prints **`Missing effects:` with an EMPTY payload** — the message is built from a label-set difference (`EffectRowDifference`) and a mode mismatch has identical labels; (3) **the recorded premise is FALSE** — the parent doc and this queue row both state `SubsumeEffectRows` treats modes as INVARIANT, but enforcement is **one-directional**: an os caller silently accepts a `seeded` *or* `crypto` callee (`c3`/`c7`/`c8` exit 0), while the reverse rejects. A control (`c4`, pure caller → seeded callee, exit 1 `Missing effects: Rand`) proved effects *do* propagate, so those passes are real behaviour, not a propagation no-op. Mechanism confirmed **by reading the types, not inferring**: `validate_effects.go:109-114` threads `declaredEffects map[string][]string` built via `ast.EffectNames` (names only, `ast.go:116-123`), and `stringSliceToEffectRow` at `:362-371` therefore **cannot** carry mode params — the required row is mode-blind for every call to a declared function. ## 114 — 2026-07-28 — Iteration 109: **RED DEV preempted the queue (Gate 1) — docs deploy fixed, dev green at `4b757f63d`.** A Dependabot 0.x "minor" bump broke `npm install` outright and had left "Deploy Documentation" red on dev ~7h. The durable finding is **why it landed**: the docs `pull_request` gate is **not a required check** and its job is **named `build`**, colliding with the required context — so it looks wired and gates nothing. Filed as **#497**. `metered=$0.00`.

**Picked**: NOT the queue's `[NEXT]`. Gate 1's per-workflow CI read found **`Deploy Documentation to GitHub Pages: completed/failure @ b8249ef35`** while CI and Build-and-Release were green — and a RED dev outranks the queue. Iteration 108's **Next (A)** (`m-effect-replay-subsumption` **M2**) is therefore untouched and remains the top pick for iteration 110; its plan, worktree and branch are still live. This is exactly the class the charter anticipates: *"time-based reds (new vuln advisories, runner-image changes, dependabot peer-dep breaks) hit whoever observes next — that's the mission's job now."*

**Reality check**: diagnosed rather than assumed, and the parent commits were checked before blaming any merge (per Gate 1). Docs-Deploy history was green through `b9186ee00` (11:29Z) and red from `b8249ef35` (20:25Z). `git log b9186ee00..origin/dev -- docs/package.json` named two commits; `git show` isolated the culprit as **#488**, `@mermaid-js/layout-elk` `^0.1.9 → ^0.2.2`. Root cause is a semver subtlety, not a Docusaurus bug: **for a `0.x` package a "minor" bump is breaking**, and `@docusaurus/theme-mermaid@3.10.2` declares `peerOptional @mermaid-js/layout-elk@^0.1.9`, so npm failed **ERESOLVE** and `make docs-install` (`make/docs.mk:27`) exited 1. Note `b8249ef35` — the previous iteration's own effects commit — is merely the first *docs-path-touching* push after the bump; it did **not** cause the red, and blaming it would have sent iteration 110 into the type system.

**Shipped**: one commit, `4b757f63d` on dev. Pins `@mermaid-js/layout-elk` back to `^0.1.9` (+ lockfile) **and** adds a Dependabot `ignore` for minor+major on that dependency. The ignore is not optional garnish: **a revert without it is simply re-landed by the next Monday batch**, so the fix would silently undo itself in six days. Patches within `0.1.x` still flow.

**Verification (first-party, reproducing CI's exact failing step)**: `npm install` **rc=0**, `layout-elk` resolved to **0.1.9**, **zero** ERESOLVE lines. The first reading of this was discarded — `${PIPESTATUS[0]}` came back **empty** because the tool shell is **zsh**, where the array is `$pipestatus`; re-run with a direct invocation and an explicit `rc=$?`. That is the charter's *"exit codes through pipes lie"* rule firing on its own terms. Then, rather than stop at install, ran a **full `npm run build` → rc=0**, which mattered: **#490** (react 19.2.8, recharts 3.10.1) merged **60 seconds** after #488, and because the install failure short-circuited the build, **its docs build had never once run green**. Fixing #488 alone could have surfaced a second, unrelated red. It didn't — but that was checked, not assumed.

**The durable finding — why a docs-breaking bump could auto-merge at all.** `docusaurus-deploy.yml` already carries a `pull_request` trigger whose own comment reads *"PRs build (but don't deploy) — gates dependency bumps that would break docs."* It gates nothing, for two independent reasons, both verified: (1) `dev` branch protection requires only `["test","lint","build"]`, and `dependabot-automerge.yml` runs `gh pr merge --auto`, which merges as soon as *those* pass — the docs run on #488 was still in flight and was **cancelled by the merge** (`gh api .../actions/runs?head_sha=23c428378…` → `Deploy Documentation to GitHub Pages | pull_request | completed/cancelled`; PR merged `13:00:32Z`, run started `12:45`). (2) `docusaurus-deploy.yml:58` declares `jobs: build:` — the **same name** as `ci.yml:315` — and required contexts match by name, so ci.yml's Go build satisfies the requirement while the identically-named docs job is silently irrelevant. `ci.yml:337`'s `docs` job is not a docusaurus build either (prompt-sync only, `if: push && ref==dev`, so skipped on every PR). Filed as **[#497](https://github.com/sunholo-data/ailang/issues/497)** with the **naive fix explicitly ruled out**: the workflow is path-filtered, so making it a required check would leave it permanently pending — and therefore blocking — on every non-docs PR.

**Gate-3b**: bounded 30-min poll, **the snippet reused verbatim once per expected workflow** (iteration 108's skill fix, first outing — no hand-rolled multi-workflow loop, no defects this time). All three workflows were EXPECTED and all completed: **CI success · Build and Release success · Deploy Documentation success**, every one `@ 4b757f63d`. The mandated direct per-workflow confirmation then **earned its keep in a way the rule did not anticipate**: it printed `origin/dev = 9d21b4469`, i.e. **dev had moved past the SHA the green runs belonged to** — two further Dependabot auto-merges (#496 `/ui`, #491 `go_modules`) landed 20 minutes after my push, the very class #497 describes. The poll alone would have reported "green" and been *literally true about my commit while wrong about dev*. A separate bounded check was armed against the new HEAD rather than inheriting an unverified tree.

**Resolving the moved HEAD, and a second finding that came out of it.** Local `dev` could not fast-forward (two Dependabot commits had landed on origin). Chose **merge over rebase** deliberately: the tree still held uncommitted rig benchmark JSONs plus this iteration's own docs-build artifacts, `git diff --name-only` confirmed **zero overlap** with the incoming files (`go.mod`, `go.sum`, `ui/package*.json`), and a merge leaves the working tree untouched whereas a rebase would have needed an autostash — Critical Principle 0 territory for no benefit. Merged to `c18ef58fa`, pushed, re-polled. **Deploy Documentation is correctly N/A for that push** (its content is `design_docs/**`, which matches no path filter) — recorded as N/A, not pending, per Gate 3b; its last real run is green on `4b757f63d`. Final direct confirmation: **CI success · Build and Release success, both `@ c18ef58fa` = `origin/dev`.** While chasing why the intermediate SHA had no runs, measured something worth its own entry: **every Dependabot auto-merge commit lands on dev with ZERO push-event workflow runs** — `a4fce855e` 0 · `07446629e` 0 · `5f90f5062` 0 · `9d21b4469` 0, against 3 and 2 for the two agent pushes either side. Likely mechanism (labelled as inference, not verified here): auto-merge enabled with `GITHUB_TOKEN` produces pushes GitHub does not re-trigger on. Combined with the PR-time gap, a Dependabot bump can reach dev with the docs build having **never completed once in either position**, which is exactly why the red stayed invisible until an unrelated commit (`b8249ef35`) happened to touch a docs-filtered path ~7h later — and why the red was attributed to the wrong commit by default. Posted to #497.

**A `test-windows` flake, diagnosed rather than assumed.** CI on `c18ef58fa` first came back RED on `test-windows` only. **Not** #494's mechanism: `--- FAIL: TestReferenceSolutions_JS/fizzbuzz (60.50s) … stderr: JavaScript execution timed out` in `internal/eval_harness`. The push was markdown + `go.mod`/`ui` deps, which cannot affect JS execution; `test-windows` was **green on the previous 7 dev runs**; and `fizzbuzz` is the cheapest solution in the suite, so 60.5s is a runner-starvation signature. Settled by evidence per iteration 108's method — **re-ran the failed job with zero code change → PASS**, all 7 jobs green. Recorded as a second, distinct site on **[#494](https://github.com/sunholo-data/ailang/issues/494)** (that issue's fix covers the `cmd/ailang` unbounded-subprocess half; this is `eval_harness`'s own timeout being too tight for a slow Windows runner). Two nondeterministic `test-windows` reds in two consecutive iterations, each initially indistinguishable from a real regression.

**Ruled out**: (1) **`b8249ef35` (the previous iteration's effects change) as the cause of the docs red** — refuted; it is only the first docs-path-touching push after the real culprit, and the failing step is `npm install`, which runs before any code is compiled. (2) **"Reverting the bump is sufficient"** — refuted by the Dependabot config: with no `ignore`, the weekly Monday batch re-opens and auto-merges the identical bump. (3) **"CI green means the bump was safe"** — this is the whole defect; CI never builds the docs site, and the workflow that does was cancelled. (4) **Treating #490's react/recharts bumps as already-validated** — refuted; their docs build had never run green, so they were built locally before being declared clean. (5) **Adding the docs build to required status checks** as the fix for #497 — rejected pre-emptively: path-filtered required checks never report on non-matching PRs and would block every non-docs PR forever. (6) **Letting either sibling-mission inbox message outrank the queue** — declined per the cross-mission contract; World's two messages are a completion report and a defect routing (`#495`), already filed by them against this repo, and neither is an ask of this loop. (7) **The `test-windows` red as a real regression, or as #494's mechanism** — both refuted: green on the previous 7 runs, a diff that cannot reach JS execution, and a zero-change re-run that PASSED; the site and mechanism differ from #494 (`eval_harness` JS timeout vs `cmd/ailang` unbounded subprocess). (8) **Rebasing to resolve the moved HEAD** — declined in favour of a merge; the tree held uncommitted rig + build artifacts and a rebase would have required an autostash for no benefit, with zero file overlap making the merge trivially safe.

**The quicksort `[3]` is not a quicksort bug — it is #505.** Narrowed first-party: `show`, `filter`, `concat`, recursion-as-argument and closure-capture-of-a-pattern-bound-variable were each ruled out (all MATCH under both engines). The actual cause is that the **VM never checks the length of a fixed-length list pattern** — `[x]` matches any non-empty list. Confirmed general at n=1,2,3: `[a,b]` swallows `[7,8,9]` → `two:7,8`; `[a,b,c]` swallows `[7,8,9,10]` → `three:7,8,9`. Only the overflow direction is unchecked (`len >= n` where it must be `len == n`), which is why it survived. Every fixed-length list pattern in every `--bytecode` program can silently return a wrong answer. Folded into the doc as a controller-verified box + **AC8b** (table-driven arity test, both directions) — because AC8 alone (exact quicksort output) is satisfiable by a quicksort-shaped special case.

**The quorum earned its fee twice, and both objections were reproduced before adoption** (the sibling mission's "a prescribed fix is a claim" rule, applied inbound). Round 0, both reject: (1) **gemini-3-1-pro, $0.018** — the doc called `tar_gzip_reader`'s duplicated stdout a benign VM_BRIDGE re-categorization; it is **unsafe replay of an effectful program**. Reproduced: the header prints **twice** under `--bytecode`, once under eval. `cmd/ailang/run_helpers.go:376` warns and then re-calls the entrypoint from the top, with no check for committed effects. Here it duplicates a `println`; the same path duplicates an FS write or an HTTP PUT (`http_put_bytes.ail` is in the corpus). Filed **#506**. (2) **gpt5-6-sol, $0.041** — the Verification Log claimed 9 Net/Clock examples and enumerated 11. Reproduced by machine-generating the inventory: exactly **9 = 3 DIVERGE + 4 MATCH + 2 EVAL_SKIP**. The cause is worth keeping: the designer counted `ai_call*` **by filename prefix**, but two of those EVAL_SKIPs declare no Net at all — the exact filename-vs-effect conflation that A2 exists to eliminate, committed inside the document proposing the fix. gpt5's replacement figures (13/12) were **not adopted** — they derived from the broken enumeration.

**The revision then found the biggest thing, and it was independently confirmed.** The parity harness always passes `--quiet` (`verify_bytecode_parity.go:235`), and `--quiet` suppresses the fallback warning (`run_helpers.go:375`). So when the VM bails mid-run the harness sees nothing, the evaluator re-runs the whole program, stdout necessarily matches eval, and the row banks **MATCH**. Controller-verified: `array_grid` (`arith MUL on Closure`), `module_let_helpers` (`arith ADD: Int vs Closure`), `map_basic` (`*eval.MapValue`), `stdlib_gzip` (`*eval.BytesValue`), `html_parser` and `std_deflate_pdf_objstm` (`TaggedValue (Result.Ok)`) — **6/6 emit exactly one fallback line**. `MATCH 149` is inflated; the first two are the *same* `arith-on-Closure` family as `array_basic`, i.e. a known bug family laundered as passing. It also explains why `VM_BRIDGE`/`VM_RUNTIME` both read 0: the non-strict fallback converts every VM failure into an exit-0 evaluator run. Note revision-0's proposed A2 fix was a **stderr sniff that could never have fired**, since the harness suppresses the very warning it would sniff for.

## 120 — 2026-07-28 — Iteration 115: `m-z3-adt-record-sort` **DOC WRITTEN, then PARKED `needs-human-review`** on quorum round 2 — and the review surfaced a **second, independent defect** at HEAD, filed as **#510** (unbounded Z3 exec). Evaluator/executor **never spawned** (a parked doc has nothing to plan). `metered=$0.148`.

**The pick.** Queue head, `[NEXT] [world-DEMAND] m-z3-adt-record-sort` (P1, clause-4/5). Iteration 114's Next offered (A) the A2 park — unavailable, no Mark answer since watermark `2026-07-27T07:53:53Z` — so this was option (C). NEW-DOC tag verified genuine (`grep -ri` found no existing doc; the designer's own duplicate search agreed, and correctly surfaced the *nearest* prior art instead). Not taken: #503 `ui-build`, which is dev-health rather than a bar item.

**Ghost discipline paid, and then the issue was wrong.** Re-reproduced first-party at `f495885b1` on a freshly built binary: `verify.errors: 1`, **exit 0**. Then bisected 7 variants and dumped the generated SMT-LIB via `verify -verbose` for three of them — and #477's cause ("emits the record's sort decl before/without the ADT's") is **false**. The record's `declare-datatype` is **absent entirely**; only `(declare-const $p_p Proposal)` is emitted. Meanwhile a **direct ADT parameter verifies**, and deliberately in its non-vacuous form (the ADT is pattern-matched in the body, not an ignored parameter) — which proves `(declare-datatype Evidence …)` emission already works and is simply never reached from the record path. That single control collapsed the encoder lane from "write an ADT encoder" to "reach the one that exists".

**The real defect is five layers deep, and layer 3 is a shipped guard.** `codegen.go:240`'s record-alias fixpoint refuses any record whose field sort is a user ADT (deliberate, per its own comment, to dodge circular deps), defers it forever, and its `if !progress { break }` give-up branch **drops it silently** → the consumer `(declare-const $p_p Proposal)` is emitted regardless → `validateDeclarations` (`codegen.go:668`), the defense-in-depth guard shipped by `m-smt-callee-sort-gate` **whose own doc claims it covers "every drop path"**, is gated on `strings.HasPrefix(decl, "(define-fun ")` and therefore never inspects a `declare-const` → Z3 `unknown sort` → `ai_check.go:167` omits `Errors` from its exit condition → **exit 0**. Fourth instance of *a gate that cannot fail*, and the first where the hole is in a guard explicitly built to close this class.

**The designer refuted one of my own "verified" facts, which is the loop working.** I handed it a section-A fact that both declaration fixpoints break silently. **False** — the second, at `codegen.go:307`, recovers via `findSCCs` + `DeclareDatatypesMutual` (Z3's plural form for mutual recursion). I confirmed the refutation at `codegen.go:326-350` before accepting it. This is the iteration-105 class landing inside a fact I had labelled VERIFIED BY ME; the provenance labelling is what made it cheap to check rather than cheap to believe. It also **shrinks the fix**: the circularity machinery gpt5 and the doc both worried about already exists and is tested.

**Both round-2 objections were reproduced before being acted on — and they did not land in the same place.** This is the iteration-111 rule (a judge's finding may be under- *or* over-stated) applied to reviewers. **gemini-3-1-pro** objected that V15's cross-boundary claim was self-admittedly "not yet empirical"; it was right to refuse it on faith, so I **ran the probe it asked for** — a fake `ailang` printing valid JSON then `exit 1`, driven through the real `RunAICheck`: `err=<nil>`, `verify.errors=1` parsed. Closed at design time by measurement, and the probe file was removed leaving the worktree clean. **gpt5-6-sol** objected that A5 was scored compliant while production solver execution is unbounded — **confirmed** at `solver.go:147-148` (`exec.Command` + `CombinedOutput()`, no `CommandContext`, no deadline, no kill, no process group; the only bound is Z3's *cooperative* `-T:`). That is a live violation of the mission's own Standing rule 6, so it was filed as **#510** on its own merits, with the impact bounded honestly: the eval harness is already protected by `waitWithGuards`, but interactive/agent use is not — and the agent prompt teaches `ai-check` as the convergence signal, so a wedged solver stalls a model session silently. Sibling Ailang World gates on `ai-check` under the `ailang-code` profile and is exposed the same way.

**Why it parked instead of using the carve-out.** gemini's objection is closed. gpt5's remaining one asks to add process-lifecycle management (context deadline, process-group kill, reap, fake-solver tests) to a sprint already sized 3–4 days. The narrow-refinement carve-out requires every remaining objection to be free of both direction disputes *and* controller judgment; a scope **expansion** is a sizing judgment, exactly what it excludes. Same reasoning as iteration 114, applied to a different shape.

**Ruled out**: (1) **Unparking iteration 114's A2 decision** — no Mark comment since the watermark; the recommendation stands untouched. (2) **`#503` `ui-build`** — dev-health, not a v1.0 bar row; deferred, not dismissed. (3) **The issue's stated root cause** — refuted by three `verify -verbose` dumps. (4) **My own claim that both fixpoints break silently** — refuted by the designer, re-confirmed by me. (5) **gemini's proposed traversal widening to map/set/generic sorts** — declined; `MapType` (`types.go:36-90`) can emit only primitives, `(Seq X)`, a bare name, or an error, so those sorts do not exist to be missed. (7) **Forcing the doc through on my own pass verdict** — Standing rule 2. (8) **A second backlog item** — Standing rule 1; this was not a bookkeeping-only pick. (9) **A weekly thread rotation** — not due: `#484` created `2026-07-27T05:27:49Z`, i.e. `07:27` **local**, after the most recent local Monday 07:00 boundary; 19/80 comments.

**Banked out-of-scope (new backlog candidate)**: `MapType`'s `TApp` branch returns `con.Name` and **discards `ty.Args`** (`types.go:56-67`), so `Box[int]` and `Box[string]` collapse to the single sort `Box`. I did not use the selector either: I used the `commits/<sha>/check-runs` escape hatch the same retro added, which is SHA-addressed by construction and stronger. The selector is **shipped but unexercised** — a claim, not evidence, in this skill's own vocabulary. Recorded in the log entry, the STATUS stamp and the PR body so the next iteration does not mistake "landed" for "proven".

**Second item (Standing rule 1: a bookkeeping pick allows a second) — `ailang#517`, the Ailang World mission's property-test finding.** Cross-mission contract applied: it does **not** outrank the queue, it gets ghost discipline, and the verdict goes back to the sender's thread. Re-reproduced first-party on a binary built from `5998f4039`. **REAL — not a ghost.** But the interesting part is that verifying it rather than accepting it changed the fix twice:

- **R-1 — the scope is not "ADTs and records".** `createGeneratorForType` (`internal/testing/runner.go:630`) has exactly two arms: `*ast.SimpleType` in {`int`,`float`,`bool`,`string`}, and `*ast.ListType`. Everything else is `nil` → skip. One file, four rows, all `tests_run=0`: `c: Color` · `r: { a: int, b: string }` (a plain record with **no ADT in it**) · `t: (int, int)` · `xs: list[int]`.
- **R-2 — the list arm is DEAD CODE, which is a second bug the filing never saw.** Both `[int]` and `list[int]` skip, because `DX-17 Phase 2` (`b9ab84e6f`, *"Normalize [T] syntax to TypeApp at parse time"*) made the parser emit `*ast.TypeApp` for both spellings and this consumer still matches `*ast.ListType`. `&ast.ListType{}` is now constructed **only in test files** (`internal/types/cycles_test.go`, `internal/gen/golang/adt_test.go`). So `NewListGenerator` is unreachable from any real program, and the only things still exercising the old shape are tests that hand-build the AST node — which is exactly why it still looks alive. This is the repo's recurring **guard-the-call-site-not-the-helper** class, the same shape as the `M-ENV-FORWARD-UNIFY` bug that recurred seven times.

**Impact bound, deliberately not overstated — the guard is half-present, not absent.** It would have been easy to write this up as "the test runner has no skip protection at all". It does. `SuiteResult.Success()` (`internal/testing/result.go:97`) is `ran > 0 && FailedTests == 0`, there is an `AllSkipped()` sentinel, there is an `--allow-skips` flag, and there is a comment reading *"An all-skipped suite is NOT success — it exits non-zero."* Measured both shapes:

| shape | `success` | exit |
|---|---|---|
| 1 pass + 1 skip | `true` | **0** |
| all skipped | `false` | **1** |

Somebody already decided "nothing ran" must be loud; the guard simply does not fire when *some* tests run — which is every real module, including both of World's. **The operational consequence is a trap worth more than the finding**: a minimal one-function repro **exits 1**, so anyone reducing this to a small test case concludes it is already fixed. Any regression test must use the *mixed* shape or it passes for the wrong reason. I put that warning in both verdict comments before anyone writes the test.

**Ruled out**: (1) **"No open `[nightly-eval]` issues" as an all-clear** — I did not accept the empty list, because an empty issue list is indistinguishable from a detector that never ran, which is the same vacuous-pass shape this iteration spent its day on. (3) **Rotating the bookkeeping thread** — `#484` was created `2026-07-27T05:27:49Z` = **07:27:49 CEST**, *after* the Monday 07:00 **local** boundary, and holds 23 comments. No rotation. The timezone stamp iteration 114 added is what made this a two-second check instead of a spurious rotation at one day old. (4) **Committing anything in the main checkout** — it is dirty with a sibling's work (`managed_agents`, benchmark JSONs, `models.yml`); everything here went through worktrees.

### Addendum to iteration 118 (same session, after the record above was merged)

Tonight's nightly fired at 05:00 **during** this iteration and filed four `[nightly-eval]` regression issues (`#520`–`#523`). Gate 0 requires every nightly alarm to be closed with a verdict, so they were triaged rather than left for iteration 119.

**All four are noise, and the run itself is invalid.** Category counts per night, from the history file:

```
2026-07-24  api_error=2   compile_error=4  logic_error=3  thrash_aborted=17
2026-07-25  api_error=1   compile_error=8  logic_error=2  thrash_aborted=16
2026-07-26  api_error=2   compile_error=6  logic_error=2  thrash_aborted=11
2026-07-27  api_error=2   compile_error=5  logic_error=3  thrash_aborted=6
2026-07-28  api_error=2   compile_error=3  logic_error=6  thrash_aborted=13
2026-07-29  api_error=42  compile_error=3  logic_error=1  thrash_aborted=3
```

42 of 42 benchmarks hit `api_error`; passes fell `52/54/61/65/54` → `14/84`. All four issues closed with this evidence; the detector defect filed as **`#524`** and queued as **`m-nightly-run-validity-gate`**.

**A hypothesis of mine was refuted, and it is worth recording because it was the *plausible* one.** These benchmarks were the first to run against `5998f4039`, which had made `ai-check` exit non-zero on `verify.errors > 0` — a deliberately BREAKING change for shell callers, landed hours earlier by the sprint this very iteration was recovering. `contract_roman_numeral` sitting in the regression list made "we broke it this morning" the obvious read, and I went looking for that. The category data killed it in one query: an exit-code change cannot produce `api_error` on all 42 benchmarks, including ones with no contracts. **Read the error stream, not the pass rate** — the same rule that says a zero-pass row is not evidence of model incapacity.

Also worth naming: this is the **fourth** vacuous-measurement finding in one iteration — `ailang#517` (properties reporting success having run zero cases), the empty-issue-list all-clear I refused to accept at Gate 1, `#524` (a detector believing a run in which nothing ran), and the unexercised Gate-3b selector. They are the same shape, and the shape is *an instrument reporting a result it did not measure*. That is now four independent instances inside a single session, which is a stronger signal about where this codebase's defects live than any one of them is on its own.

This is the through-line of the iteration, and it is the same class the last one ended on.

1. **Mine.** I told the planner, under an explicit *"I verified this myself"* label, that `tools/test_nightly_classify.py` **runs nowhere in CI** — from a grep of the root `Makefile` and `.github/workflows/`. The planner refuted it in its §0 and deleted the milestone I had invented. I confirmed the refutation myself before accepting it. **I was hunting vacuous measurements with an instrument that could not see the answer** — and I had labelled it verified, which is precisely what iteration 105's provenance rule exists to prevent. One corrupt row therefore **aborts the entire nightly reporting stage** — no verdicts, no notification, no history update, just a traceback in the launchd log. The judge was right and *under*-stated, exactly the direction iteration 111 warned about.

Four milestones, three commits, PR **#526**.

Measured cost pinned in a test: 4 of 30 persistent failures suppressed across the five good nights; `csv_to_json_converter`'s showcase escalation moves 07-27 → 07-28, **delayed not lost**, and only because the flake-guard sprint shipped `consec >= K` instead of the doc's literal `consec == K` — a refinement now load-bearing for a second reason nobody anticipated.

### The four lying instruments

1. **My own MCP probe.** First run returned an empty tool list for all five flag combinations — which reads exactly like "no tools registered". It was `rc=1`, `server is closing: EOF`: a failed handshake, not a measurement. Caught only because `addOne` was expected as a positive control. This is rule 3a's own class arriving on a **protocol handshake** rather than a grep, which is why the rule got widened this iteration.
2. **`pgrep -f "^codex"`** reported the sprint executor NOT RUNNING while it was running fine — the binary is `/opt/homebrew/.../bin/codex`, so the `^` anchor could never match. I nearly declared a dead run. Third instance of the narrow-instrument class in one session.
3. **The Go test cache.** MUT-M2 first reported `rc=0 ... (cached)` — a **false green on a mutation test**, the worst possible place for one. With `-count=1` the same mutation is red. A cached result is not a measurement.
4. **The evaluator's corpse.** Round 1 crashed mid-mutation and its last words were a fragment about rewriting a Config literal. It had left `cmd/ailang/serve_api.go` **mutated in the working tree** (`NoFeedbackTool: *noFeedbackToolFlag && false`). Commits were already pushed so the PR was unaffected, but had I read its fragment as a verdict and moved on, that mutation would have sat in the tree. **A crashed judge is not a FAIL verdict and not a PASS — it is no verdict**, and the first thing to check is what it left behind.

### What landed

PR **#529**, four commits.

- **M1/M2** — `Config.NoFeedbackTool` + `serve-api --no-feedback-tool`. **Default deliberately UNCHANGED.** The planner killed my own preferred option (make `--routes-only` mean what it says) with concrete evidence: `docs/docs/guides/agent-mcp.md:127` documents the live public Cloud Run service as `--mcp-http --routes-only --caps FS,Env` with `submit_feedback` as its one write tool, and its config lives in a **separate Terraform deploy project** — so tightening the semantics guarantees a version-skew window where the public feedback channel silently vanishes. ### The find that outranks the pick — `#535`

While measuring the before/after corpus I ran the same file three times on the same binary and got **rc=1, rc=1, rc=0**, with one property's `tests_run` varying **14 → 92**. Root cause, pre-existing: `runner.go:785-788` seeds from `time.Now().UnixNano()` whenever `Config.Seed == 0`, and `generator.go:29` sets `Seed: 0` **on a field whose own comment reads "Seed for deterministic generation"**. **No `--seed` flag exists** — `cmd/ailang/test.go` and `main.go` contain zero seed references (positive control: 3 hits in `generator.go`). The `origin/dev` baseline binary is equally unstable (`basic.ail`: rc=1, rc=2, rc=1 — note the **rc=2**).

This violates **Principle 4** in the test runner itself, makes `ailang test` unsound as a CI gate, and gives no way to replay a counterexample. It also **retroactively explains the sprint's "contradictory" measurements**: the executor and I reported different numbers for the same file and **neither of us was wrong**. ### Three claims of mine, narrowed — and the pattern in it

1. **The `case` hypothesis, killed by my own scan.** The 07-30 trial died in an 8-error cascade whose top entry says *"missing `;` … Add a `;`"* — advice that cannot work — because the model wrote `case` where AILANG needs `match`, and `case` parses as a variable. I proved that first-party with a one-token positive control (`match` → rc=0). I then suspected it was the *sustained* cause. **Refuted**: `case` appears on **one night only**; 07-26/27/28/29 used `match` correctly 3–7× and failed for unrelated reasons. Filed as `#539` **with the refutation in the issue body**, deliberately not oversold, and `#540` filed so closing `#537` didn't discard the real capability-gap signal.
2. **`#538`'s own headline was wrong**, refuted by the planner. "A strictly worse benchmark gets the quieter label" conflates *badness* with *actionability*; `m-nightly-flake-guard.md:263-270` orders the ladder by **evidence of achievability** and says GAP is excluded because "that is gap-finder territory", guaranteeing "no benchmark that has ever passed goes unpaged past its 3rd consecutive failing night". So the asymmetry is deliberate and the fix now **locks** it (mutation-proved).
3. **My proposed replacement wording was itself false — the very error class I had just filed a bug about.** I proposed the escalated filing say *"never green in the window"*; escalation is not restricted to never-green shapes, and I verified a bench with a prior **fully-green 2/2 night** escalates. Shipped wording is universally true: *"the prior window is not solid (X/Y), so this is not a certified fresh break."* **Then the correction I posted was itself wrong on mechanism** — see the reachability find below. Three layers of the same habit: stating a general claim from one confirming instance.

**Design decision (planner, both-sides).** Classifier owns the label, shell owns the message, guard becomes a tested invariant. Not shell-only (banked `class` is the trend input; CLAUDE.md §2 forbids knowingly-wrong data). **Not classifier-only** — F-1, measured: the routing block **silently drops unrecognised labels**, so M1 alone would take chronic failures from mislabelled-but-visible to **invisible**. Hence M1/M2/M3 ship as ONE commit: splitting them is not bisect-safe. `PAGING_CLASSES = {"regression","sustained-failure"}` retains the **legacy** string because live 07-29/07-30 rows carry it — dropping it re-pages tomorrow.

### Iteration 123 addendum — the metered ledger silently DROPPED this iteration's token count

Found while posting the Gate-4 chain, and measured rather than assumed. `codex` reported a token
**TOTAL** (85,774) with **no in/out split** and **no dollar figure**. `IterationPost`
(`cmd/ailang/chains_post.go:12-21`) accepts only `cost_usd` / `tokens_in` / `tokens_out`, so there
is no field for a bare total and none for "cost unknown". Rather than fabricate a split or a `$0`
(Critical Principle 2), the post carried `tokens_total` — and it was **silently discarded**:
`ailang chains post-iteration` printed `Posted iteration chain … (3 stages)` and exited 0, while
`ailang chains view` shows `Total Tokens: 0`. Cause confirmed by source: **`DisallowUnknownFields`
appears NOWHERE in the repo** (control-verified: the pattern has zero matches repo-wide), so Go's
default decoder ignores unknown fields. A success message for data that was thrown away — the same
vacuous-pass class as iteration 122's routing block silently dropping unrecognised labels.

Two corrections to my own first reading, both caught before they were acted on: (1) `ailang chains
list` shows `STAGES 0` for this chain, which I briefly read as the stages not being recorded —
`view` shows all three present, so that column counts something else (iterations 122 and world/41
show `0` too); (2) the `$0.00` in the list is **not** wrong for the control chain I compared
against — that eval ran a local model, so `$0` is true there.

**Lane: recorded, NOT patched, and deliberately no edit spent.** Iteration 116 already logged the
token-split + false-`$0` gap as instance 3 with the explicit call that it "should be designed
together with standing parked item **(0-kpi-b)**, not patched twice". This is the third face of that
same gap (unknown-total, unknown-cost, silent-drop) and it strengthens the case for designing it
once: whatever lands should add a `tokens_total`/`cost_unknown` representation **and**
`DisallowUnknownFields` so a future mis-keyed post fails LOUDLY instead of reporting success. Until
then the ledger's authoritative record for this iteration is the **log entry above**, not the chain.

That prediction was right about the mechanism and **wrong about its scope**, and the opus planner

declaration that may span many, so a plain multi-line function with **no contract anywhere**
corrupts identically (`unexpected token in expression: }`), and an `@verify` annotation — which
sits *above* `Span.Start`, so even a span-based strip misses it — yields `PAR_ATTR_REQUIRES_FUNC`.

wider corruption class. The planner also refuted `#548`'s own "known-positive control" as passing
for the wrong reason: its body `test "trivial" { true }` calls nothing, so it could never detect
that the function had been deleted.

effect annotation, since `IsPure` is set **only** by the `pure` keyword (`parser_func.go:33`) — I
verified that adding `pure` makes the AC9 case pass. The planner rejected it on blast radius and I
confirmed the reason: `internal/format/decl.go:57` is `if d.IsPure { write("pure ") }`, so flipping
the parser flag would make **`ailang fmt` insert a keyword the author never typed** — the silent
source-rewrite class this repo has already paid for once. Purity inference therefore stays **local**
to `internal/testing`, mirroring the existing precedent at `cmd/ailang/ai_check.go:231-232`.

call sites (Critical Principle 3 — one unified fix, not three patches): whole-declaration span
deletion extended upward over annotations, a local `isEffectivelyPure`, and a keep-set so the
function under extraction survives its own strip. `ExtractPureClusterForFunction` no longer computes
a stripped source the module pipeline never reads — the module path loads the root module **by
filename from disk** (`pipeline.go:157-169`), which is also precisely why the module-ful case
*masked* the bug for so long. `executor.go` 739 → **654** lines.

One mechanism, two `error_category` labels, two separate investigations. Failing sessions end `reason: "stop"` — a **clean stop, not truncation** — after ~232 output tokens with **zero tool parts**, the model's own text halting mid-sentence exactly where a tool call belongs: *"Let me first read the existing solution file to see what's there:"*.

**Four hypotheses refuted, each first-party**

1. **Lane-specific to qwen3.5** — refuted. On 07-29 hour 00, qwen3.**6** ran **18** sessions with **1** emitting tools; all 17 failures `reason=stop`, avg **236** output tokens, the same shape as qwen3.5's 232. This is the load-bearing one: it answers Mark's open question with data — switching the nightly to qwen3.6 would not have prevented either outage. Iter-128's own phrasing was correctly hedged as *suggestive*, and the hedge is what made it worth re-testing rather than inheriting.
2. **Prompt size / context overflow** — refuted, and it was *my* leading hypothesis: input `41,217` sits suspiciously near a 40960 `num_ctx`. Holding first-step input ≥41,000, the same ~41,260-token prompt yields **83/84** (07-30) and **108/108** (07-31) but **21/81** (07-29) and **2/24** (08-01) — identical size, opposite outcome — and successful sessions reach **113,373** input tokens.
3. **Model rot / missing model** — refuted. The blob is present and unchanged for 8 weeks and scored 100% the night before.
4. **Harness / opencode change** — refuted. Same opencode `1.15.7` either side, with an **identical 12-tool registry** (`bash edit glob grep invalid question read skill task todowrite webfetch write`) resolved in both good and bad sessions.

**My own instrument was wrong once, and I caught it.** The first version of test (2) aggregated `max` input tokens per session, which conflates multi-turn context growth with prompt size and made the no-tools group look capped at ~41.8k. Redone on the **first** `step-finish` to be apples-to-apples, the apparent threshold vanished and the hypothesis died. A comparison is only as good as its denominator.

**Not established, and deliberately not claimed** — the root cause. It is temporal and environment-level, pointing at ollama serving state. Same-hour co-residency of the two 37 GB models is **not** cleanly predictive (08-01 hour 01: qwen3.6 **2/2** while qwen3.5 was **3/25**), so contention is a hypothesis I refused to assert. One unverified lead handed over: the ollama **server** is `0.31.2`, up since **Tue Jul 21** (11 days), against an installed **client** of `0.32.1`.

**Ruled out**
- *"The qwen3.5 lane is broken"* (iter-128's framing) — the failure is not lane-scoped; qwen3.6 collapses identically.
- *Context/`num_ctx` overflow* — same prompt size succeeds and fails on different nights.
- *Model file missing or rotted* — present, unchanged, 100% the prior night.
- *An opencode or harness version change* — identical version and tool registry either side.
- *Model contention in the same hour* — not predictive; explicitly not asserted.
- *A code fix in this repo* — the root cause is ops-side; inventing an AILANG-lane fix would be the wrong lane per PROGRAM.md routing.

**Routing evidence** — designer, planner, executor and evaluator **all NOT fired**: triage-only, zero code changed, no design doc, no quorum. | | pid | manager | version | reachable at | loaded |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

The Fable designer specified the option-(c) bound as two budgets (`recordedDrainMaxChunks=256`, `recordedDrainMaxBytes=1MiB`) **plus a sentinel-panic abort** recovered inside the recorded op, justified as "the established Go control-flow escape … `encoding/json`, `fmt` use it internally". `cmd/wasm/effects.go:238-247` hands the Go callback to JS as a `js.FuncOf` wrapper and awaits the handler's promise via `awaitJSResult` → `awaitPromise` (`:43-53`). ## 139 — 2026-08-03 — Iteration 134: **dev CI was RED and the cause was a test helper whose own doc comment was false.** `cmd/ailang` re-linked the same 93 MB binary ~16× inside a 300s budget; on the Windows runner that package went **`FAIL 300.527s` → `ok 83.177s`**. PR **#564** → `3c28cc322`.

**Picked** — **NOT the queue head.** Gate 1's per-workflow CI read found `CI: completed/failure @ 773894d87`, i.e. dev HEAD itself, and a RED dev outranks the queue. The displaced pick (`m-recorded-stream-api` S1, plan-ready from iteration 133) is untouched and stays next.

**Reality check** — the red was **not** caused by the commit it landed on. `773894d87` is **docs-only** (`git show --stat`: one design doc, one sprint plan, one JSON — zero Go files), and `test-windows` was green on the previous **11 of 12** dev runs (job wall 337–617s). The failure was `panic: test timed out after 5m0s`, package `cmd/ailang`, stack parked in `buildAilang` → `exec.Cmd.CombinedOutput` → `go build`. Both CI jobs run `go test -timeout 300s ./...` (`ci.yml:74` linux, `:318` windows). So: a package that had been sitting just under its ceiling, tipped over by a slower runner. **The instrument nearly lied first** — a `grep -E "^\s*(--- FAIL|FAIL|panic:)"` over the 99 KB job log returned **nothing**; treated as a claim rather than a fact (rule 3a), a known-positive control (`grep -c "ok  "` → 105) proved the log was intact and a widened case-insensitive search found the panic immediately.

**The find** — `cmd/ailang/main_test.go:430` carried the comment *"buildAilang builds the ailang binary once per test run"*. **The comment was false**: no memoization, every call ran a full `go build` into a fresh `t.TempDir()`. Measured warm (compile-cached) link cost on this Mac: **5–6 s** for a **93 MB** binary, 3/3 runs. **14 call sites**, one per top-level test, none in loops. And the same package linked the same binary twice more — `serve_api_mcp_surface_test.go:29` with its own `go build -o … "."`, and `budget_scoping_e2e_test.go`'s `budgetBin`, **which was already correct** (`sync.Once` + a persistent `os.MkdirTemp` dir, with a comment explaining that `t.TempDir` is torn down when the *first* caller returns and would delete the shared binary). So the right pattern already existed in the same file tree, twelve lines of it, unused by its sibling. That made this Principle 3 (systemic fix, audit before patching) rather than three patches: one `sync.Once` builder, all three paths routed through it, `TestMain` cleaning up after `m.Run()`, signature unchanged so **no call site moved**. The 300s timeout was deliberately **not** raised and nothing was skipped — it is a real hang-detector.

**Shipped** — PR **#564** → squash **`3c28cc322`**, 2 commits (fix + changelog). Evaluator **sonnet PASS 91/100 round 1, zero blocking**, one NB (missing `[Unreleased]` entry) **actioned** rather than waved through. Measurements, all first-party:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `cmd/ailang`, this Mac (controller, **outside** the codex sandbox) | `ok 110.833s` | `ok 15.487s` (**7.2×**) |
| `cmd/ailang`, **windows-latest runner** | `FAIL 300.527s` (timeout) | **`ok 83.177s`** |
| `test-windows` job wall | 536s | 337s |

86% of the package's runtime was redundant re-linking. The Windows row is the one that matters and it is a **measurement, not an extrapolation** — pulled from the PR's own job log, not scaled from the Mac.

**Ruled out** — three hypotheses, each refuted by measurement rather than argument. (1) *"The merge broke it"* — refuted: docs-only diff, and the two `go test ./...` failures in the worktree were both proven external. (2) *`internal/effects` `TestNetHttpPost` is a regression* — refuted: reproduces **identically on unmodified `origin/dev`** in the main checkout (httpbin.org **503**), i.e. `#561`, filed by iteration 133. (3) *`internal/smt` `TestSolve_HardTimeout_FakeSolverIgnoringT` is a regression* — refuted, and this one needed real work because it **passed** on the base and **failed** in my worktree, which is exactly the shape a genuine regression has. Isolated: **3/3 pass alone** in the *modified* worktree, and the diff touches **zero files outside `cmd/ailang`** (control: the changed-file list printed alongside). The evaluator then found the leg I had missed — the file carries **`//go:build !windows`** (verified first-party, control: its sibling `solver_test.go` has no tag), so it cannot run on the failing job at all. A load flake under `./...` parallelism, pre-existing.

**Also ruled out — two local "failures" that were the repo's own guards working.** CI's anti-silent-skip gate appeared to fail locally: 2 of its 3 required tests printed no `--- PASS:`. Not a regression — `TestRunSmokeInTempDir_Pass` skips without `bin/ailang` (absent in a fresh worktree; CI builds it first), and `TestPromptCommand_Piping` skips via `internal/testutil.RequireAilangOnPath`, which **skips when the on-PATH binary is older than the newest Go source** — and I had just edited `main_test.go`. Both PASS once the environment matches CI, proven with a PATH-scoped scratch binary rather than by overwriting the shared `~/go/bin/ailang` that the rig's evals use. That guard is Gate 2's verification-protocol step 1 in mechanical form, and it correctly fired on me.

**Routing evidence** — model=**claude-opus-5** (controller) task-class=**execute** round1-score=**91** rounds=**1** corrections=**1** (changelog NB actioned) provider=**codex** agent=**codex** cost=**quota-bucket:codex-chatgpt**. Evaluator **FIRED**: `sonnet`, pinned — **generator≠judge holds** (codex/OpenAI executor vs Anthropic judge, different providers). ### The two vacuous assertions — both proven by mutation, not asserted

The executor reported **6 of 6 acceptance criteria MET** and every gate green. That is a claim, and
re-running the gates outside the sandbox confirmed all of them. What the gates did *not* show is
whether the assertions behind them can fail. Two could not.

**(1) `callbacks_test.go` — the "next callback in the chain is never entered" clause (plan AC4).**
The follow-up call was guarded on `if err == nil`, and three lines earlier the test requires `err` to
be `context.DeadlineExceeded`. So the branch is dead and `next.Load() != 0` held under *any*
implementation. Proven rather than reasoned: an instrumented marker inside the branch printed **0**
times while the test itself ran (**control: 1** PASS line in the same output). Replaced with the
strictly stronger claim that *is* provable at the runner level — on a saturated runner (capacity 1) a
follow-up call must return `ErrCallbackCapacity` with host code never entered, which fails precisely
when the token is released as the handler stops waiting rather than when the goroutine **exits**.
That is the semantics the design doc froze, and it now has a test that can fail.

**(2) `authorized_surface_test.go` — the deep-copy proof (plan AC3).** It compared `surface.All()`
against an earlier `surface.All()`. Under a shallow clone **both results alias the caller's storage
and change together**, so the comparison holds however broken the copy is. The shallow-clone mutation
**survived**. This is the sharper finding of the two, because **the sprint plan explicitly answered
this case**: *"Would still pass if the claim were false? The mutation half fails on a shallow copy."*
It does not. The plan was wrong, two reviewers and a full planning pass did not catch it, and only
running the mutation showed it. Now compared against a materialized `json.Marshal` snapshot and a
literal; the same mutation dies.

Four controller mutations in total, **each proven applied by `cmp` before its result was read** —
"the mutation didn't red" and "the mutation never ran" are the same exit code — and all reverted
byte-identical. The other two (drop the nil-`InputSchema` rejection; remove the deterministic sort)
died as intended.

discriminating, ran its own four mutations, and separately established that the runner has no slot
leak and that `ErrCallbackCapacity` is distinguishable from parent-context cancellation.

## 145 — 2026-08-04 — Iteration 140: **dev CI was red on every commit for two hours, and iteration 139 had already misfiled it as a known flake.** Fix `d434a9be9`; Gate 3b GREEN SHA-addressed on my own commit (**19** check-runs, **0** non-success). The regression was deterministic, reproducible in 0.5s, and caused by a concurrent session's curation cycle moving 12 benchmarks between tiers without updating either gate that pins the distribution.

**Pick**: **not the queue head.** Gate 1 found `CI` and `Build and Release` both `completed/failure` at dev HEAD `56b0b2a65`, and a red dev outranks the queue. The queue head (`#498` Lane B M2) is untouched and remains next.

**What was broken**: `TestAllBenchmarksHaveTierAndTags` (`internal/eval_harness/spec_test.go`) and `TestFilterBenchmarksByTier` (`cmd/ailang/eval_suite_flags_test.go`) are sibling drift detectors that pin the benchmark tier distribution. `f574c4b58` — the v0.32.0 curation cycle, landed by a concurrent non-mission session — moved 12 benchmarks between tiers and touched neither. Observed 23/23/25/8/9 against centers 23/19/21/16/9: exactly the redistribution that commit's own message declares (core 19→23, stretch 21→25, frontier 16→8). Failing on **both** ubuntu and windows, on every commit after it.

**The fix follows the tests' own written remedy**, not my judgement: *"when a shift is intentional, re-center here"* and *"don't widen tolerance — bump the target counts to match reality."* Centers moved, ±3 tolerance kept, rationale comment added to both files naming which benchmarks moved and why — as every prior re-center did, because that history is how a later reader distinguishes a deliberate ladder change from silent drift.

**Iteration 139 had already seen this red and misattributed it.** Its Gate-3b addendum states that `f574c4b58` *"failed the SAME way in the same window"* as the `#587` fizzbuzz node-cold-start flake, and used that as one of two disproofs that the M1 merge was innocent. Measured SHA-addressed, that is false in both particulars: on `f574c4b58`, `Build windows-latest` was **`cancelled`** (matrix fail-fast), not failed; the job that **failed** was `Build macos-latest`, on the tier gates — and `test` + `test-windows` failed the same way on both platforms. Wrong platform, wrong failure. `#587`'s headline conclusion survives on its other, independent disproof (`434e3e53a` carries identical M1 code and its Windows build passed), so the flake is real and the merge is still exonerated. But the cost was real too: because the red was filed as a known flake, a deterministic, trivially-fixable regression sat on dev for roughly two hours and was reported to Mark as a runner flake. Correction posted to `#587`.

**The generalisable lesson**: *two commits going red in the same window is not evidence that they failed for the same reason.* Attribution to a known flake has to match on the **failing test name and the platform**, never on redness plus adjacency — matching on co-occurrence is precisely what lets a real regression hide inside an existing issue. This is the converse of the rule Gate 1 already carries from iteration 3 ("check whether the same failure exists on the parent commits before blaming any merge"): that one stops you *blaming* a merge, this one stops you *absolving* one. Recorded as watch-item instance 1; the skill-edit bar is two, and it was not taken as this iteration's edit.

**Systemic fix (CLAUDE.md §3), because this recurs on every curation cycle**: `benchmarks/CURATION.md` is the document the curator actually reads. It mentions "tier" **36** times and mentioned **neither gate** — controls fired both ways, so the zero is a measurement. Added a §5 subsection *"Applying tier moves — REQUIRED follow-through"* naming both files, both commands, and the re-center-don't-widen rule, with the v0.32.0 incident recorded as the reason it exists. Fixing only the counts would have guaranteed a repeat at v0.33.0.

**The gates were proven non-vacuous, not assumed.** Mutating 4 `stretch` benchmarks to `frontier` reds both (stretch 21 want 25±3; frontier 12 want 8±3); reverted byte-identical (`shasum -c`, 4/4 OK) and both green again. Independently, the pre-edit failure on unchanged data already proved they bind to the YAMLs rather than to a constant.

**My first mutation attempt silently never ran, and both gates returned rc=0.** zsh does not word-split an unquoted variable, so `FILES=$(grep -l … | head -4)` followed by `sed -i '' … $FILES` passed **one** argument whose value was four newline-joined paths; `sed` failed on a nonexistent filename and nothing was mutated. ## 156 — 2026-08-06 — Iteration 152: **`assert` was a reserved keyword with NO working call site anywhere in the language — `#590` is fixed, and the sprint's own CHANGELOG entry then red-lighted a required CI context after seven local gates passed.** Pick = the queue head, the iter-145 SWEEP-BATCH row. Executor codex `gpt-5.6-sol` **hit its OpenAI usage limit mid-sprint and fell back to opus**; evaluator sonnet **PASS 88/100 r1, zero blocking**.

**The pick, and the ghost discipline that earned it.** The SWEEP-BATCH row carried three `motoko_agent` issues. `#588` was already closed. **`#589`** — nondeterministic cluster-harness failure, 6/10 — was **NOT reproduced**: the closest shape this repo can offer (`examples/runnable/pattern_sugar.ail`, 6 inline tests) ran **0/10 failures**, with a firing control (a deliberately-wrong expectation → rc=1). That is weak evidence and I said so on the issue rather than closing it: the report needs a 15-module transitive closure and **the widest multi-inline-test file here has 1 import**, so the negative is equally consistent with "fixed" and "this repo cannot express the trigger". Left OPEN with the repro burden named. **`#590`** reproduced 100% at HEAD (`v0.33.0-39-g64970c118`, both binaries rebuilt, `--version` == `git describe`) — true assert, false assert, inside and outside `/tmp`, all identical; control (assert-free body) rc=0.

**The find is wider than the issue filed it.** `assert` is a lexer keyword (`token.go:53,178,289,397`) parseable in exactly ONE construct (`parser_test_decl.go:124-125`; `registerPrefix(lexer.ASSERT)` = **0**, control **26** `registerPrefix` calls), and that construct was 100% broken — so the keyword had **no working call site in the language at all**. `assert` in a plain function body fails identically.

**And my own headline claim was REFUTED by my planner — after I had posted it publicly.** I wrote that the canonical prompt "advertises" `assert` to every eval model. It does not: line 2269 sits under **`## Reserved Keywords` — "you cannot use these as variable or function names"**, a table warning models OFF the identifier. `assert` appears **2** times in the whole prompt and never in a worked example (control: `match` **92**). That is rule 3b(i) exactly — a green citation quoted for a sentence wider than it supports — and it changed a scope call (touching the prompt became an explicit non-goal). **I posted a correction to `#590` rather than leaving the stronger claim standing**, because the issue thread is where a downstream reporter reads our reasoning.

**The design decision, made by the planner on measured grounds.** Of the reporter's three options, (a) and (b) are BOTH refuted as fixes: `internal/elaborate` has **zero** `ast.AssertStmt` handling and ends in `normalization not implemented for %T`, so registering a parselet just relocates the failure one stage later; (b) is additionally a language change needing a Conflict Surface and quorum. Option (c) is the only single-package fix — but the reporter's placement of it **in the printer is wrong**, and this is the load-bearing insight: the printer sees one node and cannot see sequencing, so printing `assert c` as bare `c` would make `{ assert false; assert true }` **pass**. Short-circuiting is a property of the sequence, so the lowering lives in the **fold**: a non-negative int sentinel chain (0 = all passed, k = first failing check), decoded in Go, entered only for assert-bearing bodies so assert-free bodies keep the byte-identical legacy path.

**A second, arguably worse defect surfaced during planning and I reproduced it first-party before filing (`#604`).** Non-final expressions in a named test body are bound to a dead `_seq` and DISCARDED, so `{ add_one(1) == 99; add_one(1) == 2 }` reports **`All tests passed!` rc=0**, while the reverse order correctly fails — a discriminating control, so it is position and not luck. This is the mission's **vacuous-pass class** again, and it is *why* the assert lowering must short-circuit. Fixing it in general is an explicit non-goal (it changes the type obligation on currently-passing tests), verified unchanged by this PR.

Read strictly, the invariant would have classed that one job as a genuine regression and pointed at a revert — the precise harm the rule exists to prevent. The better question is not "did steps run" but **"is the failure attributable to any step"**; when no step failed, nothing in the diff did.

**I shipped a vacuous pass into my own Gate-3b poll.** The first poll reported `pending=0 failures=0 SETTLED` — over a `check-runs` list of **one** (`automerge/skipped`) where **18** had existed minutes earlier. This is not a private mistake: **Gate 3b explicitly recommends `check-runs` as the instrument that "cannot drift"** — true against SHA drift, and precisely wrong during a re-run, which is the situation Gate 3b's own re-run advice puts you in. Fixed by asserting **completeness before any verdict counts** (all four expected workflows present, else `INSTRUMENT INCOMPLETE — no verdict`). Rule 3a's known-positive control, aimed at a poll rather than a search.

**The repro failed, and that is the finding's strength.** Arm C (`go test ./...`) rc=0, reported with its limitation attached — **86 of 108 packages cached, only 22 genuinely ran**, so it was a far lighter load than the issue's conditions. Arm D (`go test -count=1 ./...`) was the honest arm — **108 ran, 0 cached** — and was also rc=0. Two clean runs do not refute a flake, so I measured the variable instead of re-rolling the dice.

**The issue's stated cause is off by 3×.** The fake solver is not killed by "the 1s solver timeout": `solver.go:158` gives it `max(Timeout, effectiveTimeout) + solverKillGrace` = **3s**. Corroborated rather than merely read — the isolated arm takes **3.274s**.

**The measurement.** A probe replicating the spawn exactly (same script, same `Setpgid`, fresh `TempDir` + freshly-written script per trial), timing spawn → pidfile: idle **200/200**, mean 209ms, max 232ms, **0** over budget; under a full `-count=1` suite, **1 trial in 300 exceeded 3s, at 3.435s** (margin **−435ms**). So **~0.3% per spawn, ~0.7% per suite run** — which is why CI stays green, why it survived the CI-flake sprint, and why iteration 151 saw it once. The over-budget trial landed at load **13.6**, *not* at the higher **24.4**: a tail effect (first exec of a freshly written script), not a smooth function of load — **a fix tuned to "more load" would have missed it.**

**The same measurement refutes the issue's suggested fix.** Polling for the pidfile cannot help: a lost race means the shell was killed *before* `echo $! > file` ever ran, so the file never appears at all. Such a trial proves nothing about process-group kill — so it is now **inconclusive** and the scenario is retried, bounded at 3 with a loud `Fatalf`.

**Routing evidence:** model = **claude-opus-5** · task-class = **execute** · executor = **pi `deepseek-v4-flash-0731`** (datapoint **3 of ≥3** for Mark's new lane; probe rc=0, run rc=0, directive 7,858 B delivery-asserted, zero git writes) · evaluator = **sonnet** · designer/planner not fired. pi has **no sandbox**, so the main checkout was re-checked for out-of-worktree writes — byte-identical to preflight. `metered=$0.0063` of the $5 ceiling.

**Controller re-ran every gate and ran two mutations the executor did not**, both sha256-proven to land and reverted byte-identical: **(A)** `syscall.Kill(pid)` instead of `-pid`, breaking process-group kill, reds on **every** attempt (`child process 49684 still exists after 2s`) — the one that matters, because it proves the retry **cannot mask a real regression**; **(B)** forcing the race lost every time reds with three inconclusive logs and the exhaustion message, so that path is reachable rather than a silent pass. **Evaluator sonnet PASS 88/100 r1, zero blocking** (generator≠judge holds: DeepSeek/OpenRouter executor ≠ Anthropic judge), and it devised its **own** third mutation rather than replaying mine. **Its non-blocking finding was acted on, not filed — and it was a genuine scope error of mine**: I quoted the ~3s budget as if it covered both tests. It does not. `Z3Version` passes `versionProbeTimeout` (**5s**) directly as its context deadline, since `solverKillGrace` is only its `WaitDelay`. So the two tests do not share a budget, my 0.3% figure is the **smaller** budget's rate, and **0 of 500 trials exceeded 5s**. Corrected in the constant's doc comment (`5b06718b6`).

**Ruled out:** that two clean full-suite runs refute `#602` (they do not — the rate is ~0.7%/run, so ~1 run in 140 reds); that the flake is a smooth function of load (the over-budget trial was at the *lower* load); that polling for the pidfile fixes it (the file is never written at all when the race is lost); that every outage job shares the `steps=0` signature (one ran 17 green steps and still concluded `failure`).

Iteration 160 had left a prepared directive; per rule 3b(v) I re-derived its premises at HEAD rather than inheriting them: `config.go` present with all nine M2A symbols; the three `newRNG(config.Seed)` sites at `contract_domain.go:89` / `runner.go:261` / `runner.go:384`; the wall clock at `runner.go:667`. All confirmed by command before the executor was spawned, and the directive re-issued under a per-iteration filename with re-measured line anchors.

**THE FINDING: a test-plan row's "kills which mutation" column is a claim, and it is the one claim nobody ever checks.** §5.6's S11 row promised to kill *"guarding two sites and missing `contract_domain.go:89`"* by asserting every `PropertyResult.Seed` is non-zero, that the three differ, and that two runs agree. The executor implemented it **exactly as written**, and it passes. It also passes with the ensures site's RNG replaced by a constant — because `Seed` is stamped into each path's result **initializer**, next to the RNG construction rather than by it, so the observable never moves. Mutant asserted **LANDED** (sha256 changed) and **BUILDS** (`go build ./internal/testing` rc=0) before its green was believed. Two of three swept sites were unguarded, in a repo whose named recurring failure shape is *guard the helper, miss the call site* — and §5.1 says so explicitly, three sections above the row that failed to guard it.

The general shape, which is worth more than the instance: **an assertion that observes a value set *alongside* the mechanism cannot fail for the reason it claims.** Only one observing a value set *by* it can. Nothing upstream catches this: the plan asserts the kill, quorum reads for design soundness, the executor implements faithfully, and an evaluator confirms the row exists and is green — while the defect the row names is absent the entire time, so a real pin and a decorative one look identical.

**The repair, measured.** S11b (`TestRunner_DerivedSeedDrivesSampleStreams`) observes facts downstream of the generator: the ensures path's accept/discard counts under M1's domain filter (**192/92** at master 0 vs **208/108** at master 42) and the requires path's counterexample text (`x=-507` vs `x=-108`). Both exact and reproducible — fixed seeds give fixed samples, so this is determinism, not statistics. Mutation drill, every mutant LANDED + BUILDS asserted, source restored byte-identical each time:

| mutant | before S11b | after S11b |
|---|---|---|
| ensures site → constant seed | GREEN (survived) | **RED** |
| requires site → constant seed | GREEN (survived) | **RED** |
| `newRNG` wall clock restored | RED (S10) | RED (S10) |
